_: The five findings of the amethyst (Scoring) hero, in the house keys. Provenance: every figure in a/b is a cell of ~/Documents/cascade-scoring/releve-public.json at seal `sceau`; addresses in `source` ({table, palier, seuil, mesure}, optional `champ` naming which Rate field is displayed, or {table, compte}); re-verified mechanically at the displayed precision. Finding 01 states a deliberate design fact the record proves: geography scores zero on both sides because every written dossier resides in ordinary Union countries and no official country list was copied into the data, so risk lives in declared fields, not passports. Finding 04 shows the amethyst's reversal: here the generated variants are HARSHER than the written dossiers on the best factor, which is exactly why separation is a rule and not a convenience. `annotations` are provisional fractions of the shelving tray (eight bays, registry order, amethyst pile = recall bound, ivory pile = false alerts, brass shelf = floor): texts and fractions were measured against the delivered frames (rayonnage-reel/parchemin-01..05). One answer for the re-render: state 2 lights the tenure bay, but finding 02 is about PRODUCT: light bay three (the labels already anchor it, so they hold as-is once the light moves). State 4 keeps its own framing, the two-bay close-up.

findings.titre: Geography scores zero recall and zero false alerts here.
findings.phrase: Every file in the record sits in an ordinary Union country, because no official country list was copied into the data. The geography factor therefore scores 0% recall and 0% false alerts: the factor a vendor sells hardest carries no weight here, by construction.
findings.leg_a: recall 0% for the geography factor at 0.50, interval 0% to 8%, 42 files, all escalated
findings.leg_b: false alerts 0% at 0.50, interval 0% to 8%, 42 files, all retained

findings.titre: The product factor reaches 92.9% recall at 23.8% false alerts, at threshold 0.50.
findings.phrase: Scoring only the products a client holds reaches 92.9% recall at threshold 0.50: correspondent accounts, private banking and crypto rails carry the signal. The same factor alerts on 23.8% of the retained files, each one a review.
findings.leg_a: recall 92.9% for the product factor at 0.50, interval 81% to 98%, 42 files, all escalated
findings.leg_b: false alerts 23.8% at 0.50, interval 13% to 39%, 42 files, all retained

findings.titre: No factor's recall lower bound reaches the 90% floor.
findings.phrase: The tool holds the Wilson lower bound of recall at 90%, then takes the fewest false alerts. On the 42 files no factor reaches that floor: product's lower bound is 81%, and behaviour, at 66.7% recall with no false alert, has a lower bound of 51.6%.
findings.leg_a: highest recall lower bound, product at 0.50: 81%, interval 81% to 98%
findings.leg_b: cleanest factor, behaviour at 0.50: recall lower bound 51.6%, with zero false alerts
annotations: recall floor 90%: no factor reaches it

findings.titre: The product factor scores 79.4% recall on generated files against 92.9% on written ones.
findings.phrase: The same cell scores 92.9% recall on 42 files written and 79.4% on 126 files generated. Here the generated set is harder, and the tool still measures it on its own and keeps it out of the headline rate.
findings.leg_a: recall 92.9% for product at 0.50 on 42 files written, interval 81% to 98%
findings.leg_b: recall 79.4% at the same cell on 126 files generated, interval 71% to 86%

findings.titre: Measure the whole grid on your own review outcomes.
findings.phrase: Every rate here comes from the public record: 84 files written, 42 files escalated and 42 files retained, with 252 files generated. Two files from your systems rerun the grid, and the report lands next to your files.
findings.leg_a: 84 files written, 42 files escalated and 42 files retained, seven per typology
findings.leg_b: 252 files generated, 126 files escalated and 126 files retained, measured apart
